terms.gloss: A rule the organization must prove it followed: access reviews ran, backups restored, changes were approved. Each has an owner and evidence that goes stale.
The proof a control operated: a file with a hash, a collection day, and an attestation. The record is the product.
A short fingerprint of the evidence. If the file changes, the hash changes - which is how the auditor knows nothing was edited.
The owner stating the evidence is true for this period, and the auditor countersigning it. Both are captured on the record.
Evidence that fell short - stale, wrong period, missing - with an owner and a deadline to fix it.
How long evidence counts as proof. Stale evidence fails even when true.
Records are added, never edited. A correction is a new record that names the one it replaces.
How many years a record is kept, set by regulation, not preference.
